correctness.rationale: For all positive part sizes, a strict-majority flip decreases the finite bichromatic edge count and the only absorbing configurations are equal-bit consensuses plus simultaneous exact ties. The first part to lose its opposing strict majority determines the final consensus; independent exponential first-ring times are an exact Poissonization of uniform sequential vertex selection. Enumerating the uniform order type race gives the finite-sum kernel. Uniform order-statistic beta identities give odd/odd neutrality and even-part stochastic dominance, with the fixed-size binomial limit. Direct rational count-state testing checks 1,936 states across m,n<=8; separately implemented full vertex-state dynamics checks 7,684 states on 33 graphs. These finite tests confirm boundaries but the proof covers all sizes.

originality.rationale: The stochastic absorbing kernel, odd/odd neutral selection for unequal populations, strict even-parity bias, and fixed-size limiting winning probability are not supplied by the inspected relevant majority-dynamics literature or by accessible earlier graph-dynamics results. The historical comparison is qualified: searches and accessible full texts cannot certify priority over all unindexed work. Classical exponential-race and beta identities are credited as tools.
residual_risks: No global proof of historical priority; obscure urn-process or zero-temperature Ising literature could state an equivalent race identity.

value.rationale: Random-order absorption probabilities from opposing initial community majorities are natural dynamical harmonic measures not fixed by knowledge of possible absorbing states or adversarial update sequences. The theorem solves the complete two-parameter all-initial-profile kernel, exposing size-independent fairness for unequal odd opposing camps, strict parity bias and an exact nonzero large-camp advantage for even opposing part sizes. It is not merely a renaming of a binomial table; the graph-dynamical race reduction and tie-induced threshold change are essential.
